concepts.why: The presence of a unilocular radiolucent lesion with an irregular shape and buccolingual expansion is consistent with an odontogenic keratocyst.
The location of the radiolucent lesion at the apex of a previously endodontically treated tooth is consistent with a radicular cyst.
The presence of buccolingual expansion and a large radiolucent lesion is consistent with a unicystic ameloblastoma.
The presence of tender teeth and a radiolucent lesion is consistent with a periapical granuloma.
The presence of buccolingual expansion is consistent with an odontogenic myxoma.
The presence of buccolingual expansion and a radiolucent lesion is consistent with a central giant cell granuloma.
The presence of a large radiolucent lesion with buccolingual expansion is consistent with an ameloblastoma.
The presence of a unilocular radiolucent lesion is consistent with a surgical ciliated cyst.

rationales.F06: Unilocular radiolucent lesion is more typical of odontogenic keratocyst and unicystic ameloblastoma than radicular cyst or periapical granuloma.
rationales.F07: Irregular shape is atypical for routine periapical cysts or granulomas, suggesting odontogenic keratocyst or unicystic ameloblastoma.
rationales.F08: Buccolingual expansion with almost complete obliteration of the lingual cortex is more typical of odontogenic keratocyst and unicystic ameloblastoma than radicular cyst or periapical granuloma.
rationales.F10: The preliminary differential diagnosis included odontogenic keratocyst, radicular cyst, and unicystic ameloblastoma, suggesting these are the most likely diagnoses.
